title: A Conditional No-Hair Theorem for Transformers: How Language Models Forget Their Prompt
author: Shuyang Xiang
description: We ask how much an autoregressive transformer retains of its prompt after generating t tokens. Consider two different prompts followed by the same continuation text, so that any difference in their hidden states comes from the prompt alone, and we find that the distance between their hidden states decays approximately…
summary: We ask how much an autoregressive transformer retains of its prompt after generating t tokens. Trained models forget fast (αapprox0.55--0.7), untrained ones slowly (αapprox0.2--0.5).
takeaways: The bound holds for finite-depth pre-LN softmax transformers with bounded attention logits, under one additional condition: the pre-norm activations stay away from zero.

Cancelling the dilution with a logit bias stops the decay early in training and reverses it after, so dilution is necessary for the forgetting we measure; untrained networks and the solvable model show it is also sufficient.

The mechanism is geometric: the prompt's direct influence is diluted as the context grows, and relay --- continuation tokens passing on what earlier tokens read from the prompt --- can only add logarithmic factors.
